headline: LNG terminal outage cripples household cooking as gas crisis deepens
summary: Severe gas shortages across the capital and other regions have left many households unable to cook, with long queues forming at filling stations.
details: A severe gas crisis has emerged across various parts of the country, including the capital city of Dhaka, disrupting daily life for thousands of residents.
The shortage is attributed to an outage at an LNG terminal, which has significantly disrupted the supply chain and crippled household cooking capabilities.
Reports indicate that stoves in many kitchens have gone cold, forcing families to find alternative ways to prepare meals.
The crisis has also extended to fuel stations, where long queues of vehicles are seen waiting for gas refills.
Residents are expressing frustration as they struggle with the basic necessity of cooking fuel during this sudden supply disruption.
caption:
Kitchen stoves are going cold across Bangladesh as a major LNG terminal outage triggers a severe gas crisis.

A severe gas crisis has emerged across various parts of the country, including the capital city of Dhaka, disrupting daily life for thousands of residents.

The shortage is attributed to an outage at an LNG terminal, which has significantly disrupted the supply chain and crippled household cooking capabilities.

Reports indicate that stoves in many kitchens have gone cold, forcing families to find alternative ways to prepare meals.

The crisis has also extended to fuel stations, where long queues of vehicles are seen waiting for gas refills.

Residents are expressing frustration as they struggle with the basic necessity of cooking fuel during this sudden supply disruption.

#Bangladesh #GasCrisis #EnergyShortage #Dhaka #LNG

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: 3 staff [[two doctors and a guard dismissed]] after Health Minister's surprise visit to Satkhira
headline: 3 staff two doctors and a guard dismissed after Health Minister's surprise visit to Satkhira
summary: Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain Bokul visited three hospitals in Satkhira, leading to the immediate dismissal of staff for absenteeism and theft.
details: Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain Bokul conducted surprise inspections of Tala Hospital, Satkhira Medical College Hospital, and the Sadar Hospital on Sunday.
During the visits, the minister checked the quality of healthcare services, interacted with patients, and inspected the OT rooms, wards, kitchens, and store rooms.
Two doctors, Dr. Tonni of Tala Hospital and Dr. Sohana Selim of the Medical College Hospital, were dismissed from their posts due to long-term absenteeism.
Additionally, a night guard named Mostafa from Tala Hospital was dismissed following the theft of an air conditioner (AC) from the facility.
The minister expressed satisfaction with the hospital kitchen's food quality after tasting it himself.

During the visit, the minister also helped a visually impaired woman, Sharmin Akter, a Master's graduate from Jahangirnagar University, secure a job at the Essential Drugs Company Limited (EDCL) starting August 1st.
The minister was accompanied by District Commissioner Kausar Aziz and other senior administrative officials.
caption:
Two doctors and a guard were fired on the spot after a surprise visit by the Health Minister in Satkhira.

Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain Bokul conducted surprise inspections of Tala Hospital, Satkhira Medical College Hospital, and the Sadar Hospital on Sunday.

During the visits, the minister checked the quality of healthcare services, interacted with patients, and inspected the OT rooms, wards, kitchens, and store rooms.

Two doctors, Dr. Tonni of Tala Hospital and Dr. Sohana Selim of the Medical College Hospital, were dismissed from their posts due to long-term absenteeism.

Additionally, a night guard named Mostafa from Tala Hospital was dismissed following the theft of an air conditioner (AC) from the facility.

The minister expressed satisfaction with the hospital kitchen's food quality after tasting it himself.

During the visit, the minister also helped a visually impaired woman, Sharmin Akter, a Master's graduate from Jahangirnagar University, secure a job at the Essential Drugs Company Limited (EDCL) starting August 1st.

The minister was accompanied by District Commissioner Kausar Aziz and other senior administrative officials.

#Satkhira #HealthMinister #Bangladesh #Healthcare #Accountability

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
